changelog: Back-in-stock emails send from WP-Cron. A send job that Action Scheduler ran from WP-Cron failed with Class "WC_Email" not found, leaving its requests Notified with no email; the mailer is now loaded before an email class is named. One email that fails or throws no longer stops the rest of its batch.

Confirm and "Tell me next time too" links act on a click, not on opening. Opening one shows a page with one button; the button does it. Mail scanners that open links no longer confirm requests or turn "Tell me next time too" on.
A confirmation link confirms only the requests its email listed, not every unconfirmed request for the address. Links from 1.0.0 still work and confirm the one request they name.
"Tell me next time too" waits for the item to sell out and come back, instead of being alerted again by a later wave of the same stock or by the hourly sweep.

A restock can't stay open for good. The hourly sweep resumes an open restock whose jobs are gone (after deactivating the plugin, or a failed job) and sends alerts whose send job died. Requests still unsent after the last attempt wait again in their place, and the Restocks screen shows the failed sends in a new Failed column.

A guest's repeat ask changes nothing. It no longer overwrites the name and quantity, and with double opt-in on the reply doesn't tell whether the address is already waiting. A signed-in shopper may still update their own request.
A cancelled or refunded order gives its sale back to the restock, and a partial refund takes its amount off the revenue.
WooCommerce's Duplicate no longer copies the waiting count and expected date to the new product.
A wave that picks nobody ends its restock. An item whose last restock was cancelled isn't reopened by the hourly sweep until its stock changes.
Sizes read as the shop sets them (7.75″, not 7.75") in the form and the emails.
A refused ask (too many requests, the bot check, in stock now, or a failure) is read out by screen readers. The form also keeps its state when WooCommerce announces the same size again.
Two forms on one page no longer share id="crestock", and the signed-in nonce field has no id.
Table names go through $wpdb->prepare() with %i, including the uninstall's DROP TABLE.
The Move from Back In Stock Notifier tab says to clear the page cache after deactivating it.
The Requests list's bulk actions read $_POST.
The plugin's Description is under 140 characters.
